items.stem: How is the unemployment rate calculated?
items.answer: Number unemployed ÷ labour force × 100
items.markingKey: Labour force = employed + unemployed.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the claimant count and the labour force survey measures of unemployment.
items.answer: Claimant count: number receiving unemployment benefits (cheap, frequent, but affected by benefit rules). LFS: survey using the ILO definition of those without work, available and seeking work (internationally comparable but subject to sampling error).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each; 1 mark for a comparison [3]

items.stem: Explain why the unemployment rate may fall even if the number of jobs does not increase.
items.answer: Discouraged workers stop searching and leave the labour force, or people retire or emigrate, so the measured number unemployed falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: leaving labour force; 1 mark: reduces measured unemployment [2]

items.stem: In Umbria Nova, 24 million people are employed and 1.5 million are unemployed. The working-age population is 36.4 million. Calculate the unemployment rate.

In Marvona, 30 million people are employed and 2 million are unemployed. The working-age population is 45.7 million. (a) Calculate the labour force, the unemployment rate and the participation rate. (b) Explain why the unemployment rate might understate the true extent of joblessness.
items.answer: (a) Labour force 32m; unemployment rate 6.2%; participation 70%. (b) Discouraged workers who have stopped searching are not counted; underemployment (part-time workers wanting full-time); informal work.
items.markingKey: (a) labour force [1]; rate [1]; participation [1] (b) reason [1] [4]

items.answer: (a) 73.3% (b) Lost skills/hysteresis, lower lifetime earnings, social problems, emigration, lost output.

The number of people answering a survey
The number of people in work
items.answer: The number of people claiming unemployment-related benefits

items.answer: Fewer people are eligible or willing to claim, so the count falls although the same number are without work and seeking jobs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: eligibility; 1 mark: no change in actual unemployment [2]

items.stem: What is frictional unemployment?
options: Short-term unemployment while people move between jobs
Unemployment caused by changes in the structure of the economy
items.answer: Short-term unemployment while people move between jobs
items.markingKey: Search unemployment.

items.stem: Explain the difference between structural and cyclical unemployment.
items.answer: Structural: long-term mismatch of skills/location due to changes in the economy’s structure (e.g. decline of an industry). Cyclical: caused by a fall in aggregate demand during a downturn, affecting many industries.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each; 1 mark contrast of cause/remedy [3]

items.stem: Explain why some frictional unemployment is inevitable.
items.answer: People always change jobs and new entrants search for work; it takes time to find and match to suitable vacancies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: job changes/search; 1 mark: imperfect information/time [2]

items.stem: A graduate in Singapore takes two months to choose between job offers. Which type of unemployment is this?
items.answer: Frictional unemployment
items.markingKey: Frictional unemployment: searching between jobs.

items.stem: Car sales collapse as consumer spending falls, and car workers in Korvia are laid off. Which type of unemployment is this? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment: lower AD reduces demand for labour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment; 1 mark: explanation – lower AD reduces demand for labour. [2]

items.stem: Identify the type of unemployment in each case and explain your answer. (i) Workers in many industries in Pelora lose their jobs during a recession. (ii) Fruit pickers in Pelora are unemployed after the harvest ends.
items.answer: (i) Cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment (ii) Seasonal unemployment
items.markingKey: (i) Cyclical (demand-deficient) unemployment – caused by a fall in aggregate demand. [2] (ii) Seasonal unemployment – work is tied to the season. [2] Total [4]

items.stem: What is structural unemployment?

Unemployment due to a fall in AD
items.answer: Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers’ skills or location and the jobs available

items.stem: Many textile factories in Valdoria have moved production abroad. Explain the type of unemployment this causes and why it may last a long time.

items.stem: Newspapers in Quentara have recently reported a lively debate among economists on this issue. (a) Explain the causes of frictional, structural, cyclical and seasonal unemployment. (b) ‘Structural unemployment is a more serious problem than cyclical unemployment for Quentara.’ Evaluate this view.
items.answer: (a) Definitions, causes and examples of each type; link to AD and to supply-side factors. (b) For: Long-lasting, regional concentration, deskilling; harder to cure. Against: Cyclical unemployment can be widespread and severe in recessions and may become structural (hysteresis); both serious; depends on scale. Conclusion: a reasoned judgement on when the claim holds.
items.markingKey: (a) Indicative content: Definitions, causes and examples of each type; link to AD and to supply-side factors. items.stem: Explain two consequences of unemployment for individuals.
items.answer: Loss of income and lower living standards; loss of skills and confidence; health problems; social exclusion; harder to find future work.

items.stem: Explain why unemployment can worsen a government’s budget position.
items.answer: Tax revenue falls (less income tax, less spending so less indirect tax) while spending on benefits rises.

items.stem: In Rovania, 400 thousand people are unemployed. Each could produce output worth $40,000 a year. Each receives $8,000 in benefits and would pay $6,000 in tax if employed. Calculate the output lost each year.
items.answer: $16bn

items.stem: In Ostrelia, 200 thousand people are unemployed. Each could produce output worth $25,000 a year. Each receives $8,000 in benefits and would pay $6,000 in tax if employed. (a) Calculate the output lost each year and the annual cost to the government budget. (b) Explain why the output lost is a better measure of the cost to society than the benefits paid.

items.answer: (a) Structural (automation, unfilled skilled vacancies: mismatch); cyclical (fall in consumer spending). (b) Lost skills/hysteresis, lower lifetime earnings, social problems, emigration, lost output.
